# `protocol_wrong_role`: a role body calls another role's generated function

An `@[endpoints]` protocol generates one module per role, such as `Fan_A`
and `Fan_B`, and each module's functions take that role's states only. Passing
one role's state to another role's function is this error. It names the role
the function belongs to, the role the state belongs to, and the step the
state's role must take instead, and draws the conversation so far with both
steps marked.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO
  needs Session.Live
  @[endpoints]
  protocol Fan do
    number: A -> C : Int
    second: B -> C : Int
    verdict: C -> A : Bool
  end
  pfn role_b(s : Cap(Session.Live), st : Fan_B.Entry) : Fan_B.Yield do
    let st1 = Fan_A.send_Number(s, st, 7)
    Fan_A.recv_Verdict(s, st1, fn (_ok, st2) -> Fan_A.close(s, st2))
  end
  fn main(c : Cap(IO)) do () end
end
```

`role_b` is given a state of role `B` (`Fan_B.Entry`) but calls
`Fan_A.send_Number`, a step of role `A`.

## The fix

Use the functions of the role the body plays. `B` sends its `Int` to `C`,
then is done:

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO
  needs Session.Live
  @[endpoints]
  protocol Fan do
    number: A -> C : Int
    second: B -> C : Int
    verdict: C -> A : Bool
  end
  pfn role_b(s : Cap(Session.Live), st : Fan_B.Entry) : Fan_B.Yield do
    let st1 = Fan_B.send_Second(s, st, 7)
    Fan_B.close(s, st1)
  end
  fn main(c : Cap(IO)) do () end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

Each role only knows its own side of the conversation. A body that calls
another role's steps would send messages its peers are not waiting for. Typing
each role's states separately catches the mix-up at the call.

See also: [writing each role](../choreography.md#step-3-write-each-role).
